newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian City Hotels to buy rundown U.S. hotels.
newsitem.headline: Belgian City Hotels to buy rundown U.S. hotels.

text.p: Victor Hasson, chairman of Belgian hotels and airline group City Hotels, said Thursday his company wants to expand its hotel business in the United States -- partly by buying ones that are run down.
City Hotels, which also operates hotels in Belgium and the Netherlands, plans to invest about $100 million in the United States in the next two years by taking over and building new hotels, he said.
"It's much easier to operate hotels in the U.S. than in Europe," Hasson told a news conference to announce a 1 billion Belgian franc ($28.8 million) convertible bond issue to fund the initiative.
He said that City Hotels' strategy was to buy "derelict hotels, I mean hotels that need serious renovating."

"We can buy them now because they belong to owners in distress, who can get a reasonable price ... the idea is that we buy an old hotel, put in nearly just as much to renovate it ... and in the longer run we hope to obtain a capital gain of between 50 and 100 percent," he said.
The only condition was that the hotels had to be located in areas with strong growth potential, he said.

Hasson said factors that make the U.S. market more attractive include its higher liquidity, lower fixed operating costs and lower fiscal pressure. In addition, prices are more calculated in terms of potential profit, he added.
Hasson said he was close to deciding to buy the Royce hotel in Detroit and had bid $7.25 million.
He also offered $4.6 million to take over the Radisson hotel in Dayton, Ohio.
City Hotels is also eyeing a 202-room beachside hotel in Florida and bidding $13 million for it, he said.
The group also set up a joint venture with a U.S. promoter to build two profitable low-cost Homewood Suites.
City Hotels will invest $10 million in each of the two constructions, which will become operational early 1998. Both are located near airports -- one near Dulles.
